taxonomic_note: Current Kew POWO accepts Vernonia × guadalupensis as a natural hybrid. Some modern regional treatments emphasize that the name represents recurrent hybrid populations rather than a single independent lineage.
look_here_first: Expect an intermediate ironweed. Plants occur where western ironweed and woolly ironweed meet, with foliage, hairiness, leaf width, and head characters falling between the parents.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — UT herbarium index records Vernonia baldwinii × V. lindheimeri. Williamson — Berry Springs Park hybrid population documented by UT Plant Resources Center. Kerr — type/isotype of Vernonia guadalupensis collected at Kerrville.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Hays Purola hybrid record is explicitly introduced and is not counted.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Asteraceae head made entirely of purple disc florets; no ray florets.
best_field_traits: intermediate between V. baldwinii and V. lindheimeri
often found where parent habitats meet
mature flowering material and nearby parents are important for confident ID
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Do not force intermediate ironweeds into one parent. V. lindheimeri has narrow strongly revolute leaves with dense white hairs beneath; V. baldwinii has broader less-woolly foliage. The hybrid spans the middle.
